scope: Focused primary-source review; not an exhaustive systematic review

discovery.note: Result slots are the sum of requested numResults, not unique full-text papers. Publisher abstracts, current vendor pages and preprint revisions are labeled individually.

sources.title: An exploration to graphics processing unit spot price prediction
sources.question: Which classical time-series models fit different GPU spot-price behaviours?
sources.data: AWS GPU spot instances across regions; numeric sample coverage is not exposed in the accessible abstract.
sources.horizon: Short, middle and long term in the authors' terminology; exact step sizes were not verified.
sources.method: AR, ARIMA, ETS and GARCH compared across price behaviour types.
sources.evaluation: Published comparative exploration; accessible abstract does not establish a matching Pacific target or pinball setup.
sources.result: Authors report different winners for volatility, variance, smoothness and fluctuations rather than one universal method.
sources.limitations: Full numeric protocol and independent reproduction were not verified; reported errors cannot be compared with our scores.
sources.availability: Publisher abstract accessible; no new dataset is supplied in its data-availability statement; code release not verified.
sources.adopt: Include simple autoregression and smoothing controls; report regime and series-specific results.
sources.difference: Our fixed daily advertised-rate targets, quantile scorer and bounded selector study are a different empirical setup.

sources.title: Assessing the Current State of AWS Spot Market Forecastability
sources.question: Did AWS's 2017 pricing change alter the need for sophisticated price prediction?
sources.data: Old and new AWS spot traces, around the pricing-regime change.
sources.horizon: Cost-estimation/forecast tasks in the study; exact horizons not verified from abstract.
sources.method: Nearly 2.2 million ARIMA fits and naïve prediction approaches.
sources.evaluation: Old/new regime comparison and downstream cost-estimation example.
sources.result: Authors find much easier prediction after smoothing and strong naïve cost estimates.
sources.limitations: AWS's pricing regime and VM contracts do not establish H100/A100 market forecastability.
sources.availability: Official workshop abstract accessible; dataset/code availability not verified.
sources.adopt: Keep persistence prominent; separate stability from learned skill and report contract/regime.
sources.difference: We test a frozen multi-source advertised-rate pack; low error alone is not proof of intelligent search.

sources.title: Silicon Data GPU Rental Price Indices
sources.date: Undated current public methodology, read November 14, 2026 PT
sources.question: How can heterogeneous rental records form a comparable GPU benchmark?
sources.data: Provider rental records standardized per GPU-hour, with basis adjustments and provider aggregation.
sources.horizon: Daily index; this page is not an independently scored forecast study.
sources.evaluation: Public methodology description, not a reproducible accuracy comparison.
sources.result: Shows that normalization and like-for-like GPU price indices are established products.
sources.limitations: Coverage and proprietary methodology are vendor claims; current values are not historical benchmark inputs.
sources.availability: Public summary; underlying proprietary records and implementation not reproduced.
sources.adopt: Explicit units, contract identity, source attribution and composition boundaries.
sources.difference: We contribute an inspectable representation experiment, not invention or superiority of normalization.

sources.title: SemiAnalysis GPU Spot-Contract Composite Index
sources.date: Undated current methodology, read November 14, 2026 PT
sources.question: How can provider quotes and contract surveys form a robust rental index?
sources.data: Hyperscalers, neoclouds, marketplaces and contract survey inputs.
sources.horizon: Hourly index and contract terms; not our 1/3/7-day forecast evaluation.
sources.method: Provider reduction, weighted aggregation, composition controls, circuit breakers and bounded forward filling.
sources.evaluation: Publicly described indexing procedure; no matched forecast-accuracy test.
sources.result: An existing pricing observatory with explicit contract distinctions.
sources.limitations: Private parameters/data; survey contracts differ from advertised daily median targets.
sources.availability: Public interface and methodology; underlying commercial dataset restricted.
sources.adopt: Separate contracts and missingness; a polished chart is product work rather than research novelty.
sources.difference: Our official targets remain unchanged; we do not rank our forecasts against this commercial index.

sources.title: Probabilistic Forecasts, Calibration and Sharpness
sources.question: How should predictive distributions be diagnosed?
sources.data: Continuous forecasts, including a wind-energy case study.
sources.method: Calibration and sharpness diagnostics with proper forecast evaluation.
sources.result: Concentrated predictions are useful only when considered alongside calibration.
sources.limitations: A nominal interval level does not prove empirical coverage; our three dates cannot establish population calibration.
sources.availability: Publisher summary accessible; article describes diagnostic tools.
sources.adopt: Show observed coverage, sample counts and interval width together, without a calibration certificate.
sources.difference: We apply descriptive diagnostics to stored q10–q90 policy results, without changing the scorer.

sources.title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice — time-series cross-validation
sources.type: Authors' methodological textbook and reproducible examples
sources.question: How can forecast errors be measured without training on the future?
sources.data: Illustrative time series in the book's forecasting workflow.
sources.method: Chronological training windows and future test errors; compare with simple benchmarks.
sources.evaluation: Methodological explanation and executable examples, not a competing GPU score.
sources.result: Future observations must remain outside each training origin; fit error is not forecast error.
sources.limitations: A row timestamp alone does not establish data vintage; our final dates were already inspected.
sources.availability: Open textbook and associated R examples.
sources.adopt: Expose origin, label maturity and retrospective reuse in the interface and ledger.
sources.difference: Our pack/access constraints require additional vintage and publication caveats.

sources.title: Conformalized Quantile Regression
sources.question: Can regression intervals be both adaptive and coverage-valid?
sources.horizon: Prediction intervals for new samples; not a temporal GPU forecast horizon.
sources.method: Quantile regressors plus held-out conformal calibration; comparisons with other conformal methods.
sources.evaluation: Finite-sample theory and empirical regression studies.
sources.result: Authors obtain adaptive intervals with coverage guarantees under exchangeability.
sources.limitations: Exchangeability does not automatically hold for dependent rental time series; no such guarantee is claimed here.
sources.adopt: Distinguish nominal q10–q90 bands from measured coverage and from assumption envelopes.
sources.difference: We diagnose frozen intervals; we do not retrofit conformal calibration on the opened evaluation.

sources.title: Meta-Learning Acquisition Functions for Transfer Learning in Bayesian Optimization
sources.question: Can prior tasks teach a better next-experiment acquisition rule?
sources.data: Synthetic functions, hyperparameter problems and simulation-to-real transfer.
sources.horizon: Sequential function-evaluation budget, not calendar forecast time.
sources.method: RL-trained acquisition behaviour within a Gaussian-process BO loop.
sources.evaluation: Transfer across related optimization tasks against general acquisition rules.
sources.result: Authors report data-efficiency benefits when transferable structure exists.
sources.limitations: Different spaces, training information and budgets; no direct score ranking with our selector.
sources.availability: Paper accessible; implementations must be credited if reused.
sources.adopt: Treat learned experiment selection as established; compare information and online budgets explicitly.
sources.difference: Our categorical small-model study uses 42 fixed candidates and six result reveals.

sources.title: MetaDistill: Unlocking the Performance Ceiling for Pretrained Optimizers
sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference paper and official code
sources.question: Do diverse expert optimization trajectories improve learned optimizers?
sources.data: BBOB test suite and three control tasks.
sources.horizon: Optimization evaluation budgets; no rental-price horizon.
sources.method: Expert-trajectory distillation and optional test-time self-supervised refinement.
sources.evaluation: Learnable-optimizer comparisons across unseen objective landscapes.
sources.result: Authors report improved generalization relative to original training paradigms.
sources.limitations: Our narrow teacher and repeated dates do not reproduce that transfer claim.
sources.adopt: Audit teacher quality and distinguish learned method priors from feedback use.
sources.difference: We keep teacher-alignment failures and no-observation ties visible; no superiority claim.

sources.title: MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering
sources.question: Can agents perform real ML engineering tasks?
sources.data: 75 Kaggle competitions with task-specific data and human leaderboard references.
sources.method: Agent scaffolds and model comparisons, resource scaling and contamination analysis.
sources.evaluation: Held-out competition grading and repeated runs.
sources.result: Establishes an inspectable engineering benchmark; its medal rates are not comparable with pinball loss.
sources.limitations: Our bounded arm selection is much narrower than writing and training arbitrary ML systems.
sources.adopt: Record reproducibility, resources, unsuccessful trials and contamination limits.
sources.difference: We study a domain-specific result-reveal process, not general end-to-end ML engineering.

sources.title: AI Research Agents for Machine Learning: Search, Exploration, and Generalization in MLE-bench
sources.question: How do search policies and operators interact in research agents?
sources.horizon: Bounded search/engineering budget rather than a forecast horizon.
sources.method: Greedy, MCTS and evolutionary search with controlled operator choices.
sources.evaluation: Operator/search ablations and validation-to-test generalization analysis.
sources.result: Authors report gains from joint design and a consequential validation-selection gap.
sources.limitations: Their leaderboard results use different tasks and resources; selection overfit remains a concern here.
sources.adopt: Separate changed actions, changed final choices and changed future loss.
sources.difference: Our feedback diagnostics inspect fixed recorded traces, not a replication of AIRA.

sources.title: MLS-Bench: A Holistic and Rigorous Assessment of AI Systems on Building Better AI
sources.question: Can AI invent methods that generalize across settings and scales?
sources.data: 140 tasks across 12 domains according to the authors.
sources.horizon: Controlled transfer/scaling evaluations; not a calendar forecast target.
sources.method: Targeted component improvements and cross-setting evaluation.
sources.evaluation: Generalization and scalability separated from engineering-style tuning.
sources.result: Authors find robust method invention more difficult than local tuning.
sources.limitations: Our three reused dates and fixed methods cannot establish method discovery.
sources.adopt: Narrow claims to bounded selection and state the independent-evaluation gap.
sources.difference: We demonstrate a transparent empirical pipeline rather than general scientific invention.

sources.title: ForecastBench: A Dynamic Benchmark of AI Forecasting Capabilities
sources.question: How can forecasting systems be evaluated on outcomes unknown at submission?
sources.data: Regularly refreshed future-event questions with automatic resolution.
sources.method: Pre-resolution forecast commitments, automated scoring and human/system comparisons.
sources.evaluation: Future-only submissions, unlike reused historical test periods.
sources.result: Provides a design for contamination-resistant prospective evaluation; not our quantile-price scorer.
sources.limitations: Event probabilities and Brier-style evaluation cannot be substituted for Pacific pinball loss.
sources.adopt: Keep prospective commitments pending until outcomes mature; distinguish them from hindcasts.
sources.difference: Our future manifest uses stale November 6 inputs and cannot yet demonstrate accuracy.

sources.title: Forecasting for monetary policy making and communication at the Bank of England: a review
sources.type: Independent institutional review, not a forecasting algorithm paper
sources.question: How can forecasting infrastructure and public uncertainty communication improve?
sources.data: Review of the Bank's processes and communication, not a common GPU dataset.
sources.horizon: Macroeconomic policy horizons; not directly comparable.
sources.method: Institutional review of forecasting, risk analysis and communication.
sources.evaluation: Recommendations and historical-process assessment, not an interface A/B experiment.
sources.result: Recommends stronger error learning and risk communication; the full review critiques existing fan charts.
sources.limitations: Does not prove that our interface improves comprehension.
sources.availability: Official landing page and publicly linked full review.
sources.adopt: Explain what changes a scenario; show uncertainty limits and measured forecast errors plainly.
sources.difference: Our assumption paths have no probabilities and remain visually separate from submitted quantiles.

sources.title: Explorable Explanations
sources.question: How can readers actively test an author's assumptions?
sources.data: Reactive explanatory examples; not a price dataset.
sources.method: Manipulable assumptions, immediate calculation feedback and contextual explanation.
sources.evaluation: Design argument and prototypes; not a controlled usability result.
sources.result: Demonstrates the pattern of a document as an environment for thinking.
sources.limitations: We must measure our own comprehension/accessibility; copying a visual style is not validation.
sources.adopt: Live margin notes and pinned calculations that preserve their assumptions and provenance.
sources.difference: Our notebook binds interactions to actual frozen forecasts and explicit compounded scenarios.

contribution: An auditable empirical study of advertised GPU rental rates and bounded experiment selection, with explicit information, cost and evaluation limits.
not_claimed: First GPU price forecast or normalized index
Matched superiority over commercial indices or published agent leaderboards
